A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SA-DPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–P are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination and terminology changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synonym stress tests, Anthropic HH-RLHF loss comparisons, and UltraFeedback ranking results in Section 7, Tables 1–3, and Appendix M.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original Argilla/Qwen ranking results, margin-satisfaction measurements, and a downstream generation comparison in Sections 6.1 and 7.3.

M1.justification: The margin-shifted surrogate and SA-DPO objective, including the semantic-distance margin Γ(y,y′) = τ∆(y,y′), remain unchanged. The Qwen experiments apply the existing method; the appendix preference-model renaming changes no algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds Argilla DPO-Mix-7k preference evaluation and open-ended conversational generation using MT-Bench-style prompts. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained synonym, HH-RLHF, and UltraFeedback experiments by evaluating generated responses as well as preference ranking.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments: DPO versus SA-DPO for synonyms, DPO/IPO/Poly-3 for capacity analysis, and DPO/SimPO/SA-DPO for UltraFeedback. Argilla and margin-satisfaction comparisons reuse DPO and SimPO; the new generation comparison reuses DPO.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, an Argilla fine-tuning protocol, PairRM head-to-head win-rate evaluation on 200 held-out prompts, and a margin-satisfaction metric. These substantially expand the experimental design. The reported settings of the existing controlled and UltraFeedback experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 adds a targeted diagnostic using margin satisfaction as a proxy for the approximation gap, reporting 58.0% for DPO, 63.0% for SimPO, and 72.3% for SA-DPO. The existing synonym-stability and loss-tail analyses retain their original questions and designs.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 change from point estimates without stated run counts to loss and accuracy summaries with mean ± standard deviation over five runs. Table 3 already used five-run uncertainty reporting in v1. This establishes expanded reporting, not an explicit increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds Argilla ranking results, margin-satisfaction results, and a 58.5% generation win rate against DPO. In Table 2, DPO/IPO/Poly-3 accuracies change from 71.8/94.7/100.0% to five-run means of 71.6/94.5/99.7%; Table 1's DPO loss changes from 0.1684 to 0.1695. UltraFeedback Table 3 remains unchanged. The additions and revised summaries do not establish a same-setting performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, theorems, derivations, and appendix proofs are retained. Section 4 expands the h± notation, and Definition N.2 renames the Generalized Bradley-Terry Model to the Surrogate-Induced Preference Model without changing its equations. The additional assumption discussion is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion newly emphasize superiority over DPO and SimPO across datasets and architectures, plus the 58.5% downstream generation win rate. The central contributions concerning inconsistency, margin shifts, SA-DPO, and the loss-tail hierarchy remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly acknowledges that its equicontinuity condition is weaker and non-standard relative to uniform equicontinuity. Sections 6.1 and 7.3 add interpretations linking margin satisfaction to reduced capacity penalties and generation performance to prevention of hallucinated conversational artifacts. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendix M adds Qwen settings: LoRA rank/alpha 32, 1,000 steps, batch size 16, learning rate 5×10^-5, and the 200-prompt PairRM evaluation. Conversely, Section 7.3 removes the explicit UltraFeedback median-distance cutoff of 0.1565 while retaining the median-split rule; this is reduced disclosure, not evidence of a changed split.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 adds explicit attribution of the inconsistency result and proof technique to Mao et al. (2023c, Theorem 2.1). Appendix A expands recent consistency and deferral references, and new experimental resources receive citations. The main organization and research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, introduction opening, and conclusion; expands explanations of minimizability gaps and assumptions; numbers the contributions; and adds acknowledgments. It also consistently renames the appendix preference model. The main section and appendix order is preserved.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are enlarged, and Tables 1–2 receive revised captions and sizing for uncertainty reporting. Figures and tables reflow with the expanded text. Both versions retain the same three figures and four tables, with unchanged diagram and plotted-curve content.

improvement.justification: The Argilla/Qwen and generation evaluations broaden v1's existing empirical validation, while five-run uncertainty in Tables 1–2 and clearer assumption wording and attribution improve assessability. These are useful but limited gains: the new margin-satisfaction threshold is unspecified, and the aggregate PairRM win rate does not directly test the claimed prevention of hallucinated artifacts.
